solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Adam's disturbed about article that's seen on front of Times?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the rearranged name is wrapped around the article
letters that are disturbed are thrown out of their order, so the letters of the name are rearranged

parts.note: the definite article is the word the

explanation.surface: Someone named Adam is upset over a piece printed on the newspaper's front page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' is the newspaper itself, so the definition is self-referential: the name printed at the top of this very paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The title block printed across the top of a newspaper's front page is its masthead, so it is what appears there.

clue.text: Protester showing some hesitation after a month

indicators.note: after places the hesitation sound behind the month

parts.note: March is the third month of the year
er is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: A demonstrator dithers a little after several weeks.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes on a protest march is a demonstrator, a protester on foot.

clue.text: American looking up little Daniel in African state

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: US is short for American, as in US citizen
Dan is a shortened form of Daniel

explanation.surface: An American visits a young Daniel living in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking up' turns US to SU, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a country in north-east Africa, so it is one example of an African state.

clue.text: Wear this red crumpled fabric

indicators.note: crumpled cloth is pushed out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to put on a creased red garment.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a hand-woven woollen cloth from the Outer Hebrides of Scotland, a named fabric.

clue.text: Apprehend a wrongdoer at last, then relax

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word

parts.note: to rest is to relax

explanation.surface: Catch a criminal finally, and then take it easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Police apprehend a suspect by arresting them; both mean to seize and take into custody.

clue.text: Boast from British newspaper

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: A British paper is crowing about something.
explanation.definitionFit: To brag is a direct synonym of to boast, both meaning to talk with excessive pride.

clue.text: Take over from sappers wanting time off, say

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are the British Army's sappers

indicators.note: say signals that the word for time off is matched by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: leave is time away from duty

explanation.surface: Army engineers who want a break are covered by others, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' means LIEVE is spelt to sound like LEAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone is to take their place on duty so they can rest.

clue.text: Fantastic Greek nosh

parts.note: nosh is British slang for food, and as a verb means to eat

explanation.surface: Wonderful Greek grub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nosh' looks like a noun for food but gives the verb EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal terms of praise, meaning wonderful or excellent.

clue.text: Haggard traveller?

parts.note: reads as a worn-out wayfarer, but recalls the novelist H. ... Haggard, whose middle name is also a word for someone on horseback

explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' looks like an adjective meaning gaunt, but it is the surname of H. Rider Haggard, author of King Solomon's Mines; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who travels on horseback or a bike is a rider, and it is also Haggard's middle name.

clue.text: Do crossword again, showing determination

definitions.meaning: to solve a puzzle once more
firmness of purpose, a fixed intention

explanation.definitionFit: Resolve is a noun for firm determination, and split as re-solve it means work out the puzzle a second time.

clue.text: Cocktail shared at first with group of workers and chauffeur

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word

parts.note: a crew is a team working together, as on a ship
a chauffeur is a hired driver

explanation.surface: A drink is split between a work team and their driver.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a mixed drink of vodka and orange juice, so it is one example of a cocktail.

clue.text: She supplies eggs and ham every night, for starters

indicators.note: starters are the opening items, so the first letter of each of these three words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone describes a cook who serves eggs and ham each evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A female chicken is the bird that lays eggs, so the clue's 'she' is a laying bird.

clue.text: Almost guarantee fellow is rebellious type

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to insure something is to guarantee against its loss
gent, short for gentleman, is a word for a fellow or man

explanation.surface: A near guarantee that some chap is a rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent is a person who rises in revolt against authority, a rebel.

clue.text: Where motel not entirely off the beaten track

indicators.note: only part of the words is used, so the run of letters sits inside them

explanation.surface: Asking where a motel is that is not quite out in the wilds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' picks letters from inside wheRE MOTEl.
explanation.definitionFit: A place off the beaten track is isolated and far from main routes, which is what remote means.

clue.text: Claim he changed name

indicators.note: changed letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone asserts that he altered what he is called.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common boy's first name, so it is an example of a name.

clue.text: Pious type's eating tiny candies

indicators.note: something eating another takes it inside, so the abbreviation holds the small word

parts.note: a pious type is a saint, abbreviated ST, and the possessive adds S
wee is Scottish and informal for tiny

explanation.surface: A devout person is nibbling little sugary treats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' holds WEE inside the saint's abbreviation with its possessive S, which is why the clue says 'type's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Candies is the American word for sweets, the British term for confectionery.

clue.text: FBI officers appearing in set piece

indicators.note: the agents show up inside the other word

parts.note: taken as written
G-men, short for government men, is slang for FBI agents

explanation.surface: Federal agents turn up in a staged scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing in' is the container signal; G-men is old American slang for government agents of the FBI.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is a section or portion of a whole, a piece of it.

clue.text: Sailors in part of ship, the centre

indicators.note: in places the sailors inside the ship's part

parts.note: the keel is the structural spine along the bottom of a ship
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: Seamen are positioned in the middle section of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'the centre' looks like a link to the ship but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A kernel is the core or essential heart of something, its centre.

clue.text: Conman in fuss, always

parts.note: a racket is a din or commotion, a fuss
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A swindler is forever causing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer runs dishonest schemes to make money, so is a kind of fraudster or swindler.

clue.text: Trace different answer in response

indicators.note: a different form of the word is a rearrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Track down another reply.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to behave or reply as a result of something, which is answering in response.

clue.text: Flag Salvation Army placed near front of graveyard

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Salvation Army banner is set up beside a cemetery entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a noun for a banner, but here it is the verb meaning to tire.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to droop or lose energy, and to sag is likewise to sink or weaken.

clue.text: In early season, there's no new growth of holly?

indicators.note: no here means without, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: spring is the early season of the year

explanation.surface: Holly puts out no fresh shoots in the early part of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no new' removes N from SPRING; the question mark marks holly as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small shoot or twig, such as a piece of holly used for decoration.

clue.text: A boy appearing with daughter in pantomime

parts.note: a lad is a boy
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy and a girl take part in a festive stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: A pantomime is a British Christmas stage show based on a fairy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: The story of the boy with the magic lamp is a classic British pantomime title, so it names one example.

clue.text: Poetry volume seer translated

indicators.note: translating changes the form of something, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A book of poems by a prophet has been put into another language.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is writing arranged in metrical lines, which is poetry.

clue.text: It is used in postnatal care

definitions.text: It is used in postnatal care

indicators.note: the letters needed are contained within the following words

explanation.surface: Something is applied in looking after a newborn baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' points to letters inside postnaTAL Care; the whole clue also describes baby powder.
explanation.definitionFit: Talcum powder is dusted on babies to keep their skin dry, so it features in caring for newborns.

clue.text: Not a socialist to be seen, OK?

definitions.text: Not a socialist to be seen
definitions.meaning: if every person present is right-wing, none is a socialist

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an everyday way to say things are acceptable, and read literally it says everyone leans politically right.
